title: Divergence report — the comparator's output contract
description: Benchmark protocol layer, non-normative. Categorical throughout: there is no similarity score and no distance measure, because at n=2 repeatability is characterised rather than estimated and a number here would be an unjustified one. Note what the contract makes impossible: there is no field an aggregate verdict could occupy, and `findings: []` is meaningful only alongside `arms`, so an absent result can never be serialised as a clean one.

protocol_commit.description: The commit at which the frozen protocol was published, before any arm ran. Null means the comparison was run unpinned — a development run, never a result.

arms.description: Arms that survived the benchmark protocol gate. Fewer than two means no cross-runtime comparison was possible, and the report says so rather than reporting no findings.

within.description: Per-arm repeat comparison. `not-measured` where an arm ran once: repeatability is a measured variable, and where it was not measured nothing about it is claimed.

rejected.description: Benchmark protocol layer. These arms failed to REPORT properly; nothing here is a finding about a runtime.

runtime_findings.description: MTDR contract layer. These arms emitted non-conformant MTDR artefacts — a finding about the runtime — and remain in the comparison so the divergence can be located.

sample_label.description: Assigned mechanically from the divergence matrix, never by hand.

classification.description: Rendered from a classification.schema.json entry. Absent means unclassified, which is an open finding rather than a resolved one.
